title: refactor(hub): sign the GitHub App setup state instead of storing it
body:
## What changed

- The manifest `state` is an HMAC-SHA256 token (key derived from `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` under a fixed label) carrying tenant, principal, user, session, credential and provider ids, a nonce and a 10 minute expiry. The callback verifies signature (constant time), expiry, and the signed-in user and session.
- Duplicate conversions: GitHub converts a code once; under the tenant lock a fresh setup inserts only while no credentials exist, and a replacement writes only while both credentials' `updatedAt` match the values signed at start.
- Removed `corbits_github_manifest_state`, its startup migration, the cancel route and the portal's setup-in-progress UI. SELF_HOST.md gets the `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS corbits_github_manifest_state;` upgrade note.

## Verification

- `bun run check`, `bun run test` (689 pass, Postgres).
- New tests: signed state round-trip; tampered, foreign-key and expired states refused; another user's state refused before any database or GitHub call; concurrent and replayed callbacks for both fresh and replacement setups commit once even when GitHub converts the code every time.
author: TheGreatAxios
commits: refactor(hub): sign the GitHub App setup state instead of storing it
